This is truly incredible. I was trying to explain to my girlfriend why this is so important. To her, it looks nifty, but she has a hard time grasping the true importance of it.

The best I was able to sum it up, is that a re-usable first stage, along with a re-usable second stage, would cut the cost of putting things in orbit by an entire order of magnitude. To put that in perspective, it's the difference between our internet costing $600 a month which is insane, and $60. If the internet costs $600 a month, far fewer people would afford it, and there would be no twitter, no facebook, no Youtube, no Amazon. Bringing the costs down and making it more broadly accessible makes all sorts of crazy things we never imagined possible.

Likewise, bringing the cost to put things in orbit down by an order of magnitude allows many more companies access to space. It allows people to try riskier ventures. It allows people to iterate on ideas faster and cheaper. It's one step closer to whatever insane innovations might come of micro gravity manufacturing. We could develop crazy new materials, with previously unknown superconducting properties, or tensile strength, or other extreme properties.

As far as I'm concerned, it's the next great technological revolution.
